target.title: [security] Tencent Cloud redirects can disclose session tokens and cloud-init credentials
target.body:
# [security] Tencent Cloud redirects can disclose session tokens and cloud-init credentials

## Summary

The Tencent Cloud provider signs API requests and dispatches them through an HTTP client without an origin-confining redirect policy. Go therefore follows redirects under its default rules.

For 307 and 308 responses, Go preserves the POST method and body. An unrelated redirect origin receives the complete Tencent Cloud API payload and the custom `X-TC-Token` session-token header. Go removes `Authorization` for unrelated hostnames but retains it for the original hostname and its subdomains, without treating an effective-port change as a credential boundary. Those destinations also receive the signed `Authorization` header containing the SecretID.

The replayed RunInstances body includes infrastructure metadata and base64-encoded cloud-init UserData. When Tailscale bootstrapping is enabled, that UserData contains the Tailscale authentication key. This violates Crabbox's documented rule that credentialed redirects remain on their configured origin. Exploitation nevertheless requires a separate ability to influence a redirect response from a trusted HTTPS API endpoint; no deployed Tencent Cloud open redirect or service compromise was tested or established.

## Affected Components

- `internal/providers/tencentcloud/client.go:70-89` selects the supplied HTTP client or constructs a default client without adding a `CheckRedirect` guard.
- `internal/providers/tencentcloud/client.go:184-229` serializes each API request, signs it, and calls `httpClient.Do` before evaluating the final response status.
- `internal/providers/tencentcloud/client.go:286-324` places the SecretID in `Authorization` and the temporary-credential token in the custom `X-TC-Token` header.
- `internal/providers/tencentcloud/config.go:127-158` resolves the configurable CVM endpoint and the separate Tag and STS endpoints without establishing redirect boundaries.
- `internal/providers/tencentcloud/backend.go:166-190` constructs RunInstances UserData and includes network, security-group, tag, and instance configuration in the request.
- `internal/cli/bootstrap.go:40-115` constructs the cloud-init document embedded in UserData.
- `internal/cli/bootstrap.go:1602-1679` embeds the configured Tailscale authentication key in cloud-init when Tailscale bootstrapping is enabled.
- `internal/providers/tencentcloud/provider_test.go:65-141` contains existing upstream request-building and signing tests, but no upstream redirect coverage.
- `README.md:66-72` documents same-origin confinement as the expected boundary for credentialed HTTP redirects.

## Attack Path

1. An operator configures valid Tencent Cloud credentials and invokes an operation that reaches the CVM, Tag, or STS API. RunInstances is the highest-impact path because it carries cloud-init UserData.
2. An attacker can influence the trusted HTTPS endpoint's response so that it returns a 307 or 308 redirect to an attacker-controlled destination. This could require an open redirect, routing-layer compromise, malicious trusted proxy, or comparable control over the endpoint response; none is demonstrated against the deployed Tencent Cloud service.
3. The provider attaches `Authorization` and, for temporary credentials, `X-TC-Token`, then dispatches the POST through an unguarded client.
4. Go follows the redirect and replays the body. Any unrelated origin receives the body and `X-TC-Token`. A controlled subdomain or destination using the original hostname on another port also receives `Authorization`.
5. For RunInstances, the body exposes instance configuration, VPC and subnet identifiers, security-group IDs, tags, the SSH public key, and any Tailscale authentication key embedded in cloud-init.

The operator must perform an ordinary provider operation. Default endpoints use HTTPS, preventing a passive network observer from injecting redirects without defeating TLS or controlling a trusted endpoint. A caller-supplied HTTP client with an already strict redirect policy can also prevent the replay.

## Impact

A successful redirect can disclose a Tencent Cloud STS session token and signed request payloads to an unrelated origin. The session token and exposed SecretID are not sufficient to authenticate Tencent Cloud API calls without the SecretKey, which is never transmitted.

The more consequential deployment-dependent exposure is the cloud-init payload. When Tailscale support is enabled, it contains the Tailscale authentication key, which may allow unauthorized device enrollment subject to that key's tags, reuse policy, expiry, and provider-side controls. Other exposed data includes infrastructure identifiers, lease metadata, instance configuration, and the SSH public key.

Go drops the POST body for 301, 302, and 303 redirects, and strips `Authorization` for unrelated hostnames. The default redirect limit is ten hops. These controls reduce exposure but do not protect `X-TC-Token`, 307/308 bodies, subdomains, or different ports on the same hostname.

## Severity Assessment

### CVSS Assessment

| Metric | v3.1 | v4.0 |
|--------|------|------|
| **Score** | 5.3 / 10.0 | 6.0 / 10.0 |
| **Severity** | Medium | Medium |
| **Vector** | CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N | CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N |
| **Calculator** | [CVSS v3.1 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N) | [CVSS v4.0 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/4.0#CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) |

The scores reflect a network-delivered redirect, no attacker privileges in Crabbox, and an operator invoking the provider. CVSS v3.1 uses High attack complexity because the attacker must influence a trusted HTTPS endpoint and Required user interaction because an operator must initiate an API operation. CVSS v4.0 represents the endpoint-control prerequisite as AT:P, with passive interaction and no further exploitation complexity once a redirect can be supplied. Scope remains within the vulnerable client for the scored disclosure; confidentiality can be high when cloud-init contains a Tailscale authentication key, while direct integrity and availability impacts are none. HTTPS, redirect influence, optional Tailscale use, credential expiry and scope, unrelated-host Authorization stripping, and caller-supplied redirect policies are material preconditions and countercontrols.

## Recommended Remediation Approach

Clone the effective HTTP client and install a Tencent Cloud-specific redirect policy that permits a hop only when its scheme, canonical hostname, and effective port match the origin of the request that initiated the redirect chain. Comparing against the initiating request handles the provider's distinct CVM, Tag, and STS origins without treating redirects between them as trusted.

Preserve any caller-supplied `CheckRedirect` policy and retain Go's default ten-hop limit when no policy was supplied. Avoid mutating a shared client. Return a stable, redacted error for rejected redirects because Go otherwise wraps `CheckRedirect` errors with the untrusted Location URL.

Add regression coverage for unrelated-origin, subdomain, different-port, and cross-service 307 redirects; same-origin redirects; preservation of caller policy and the default redirect limit; and redaction of rejected destinations. Negative assertions should prove that neither credentials nor request bodies reach rejected origins.

## Validation

Validation used the current source at commit `8b686531ece6` and a focused transport-level test added only to the disposable checkout. The test constructed the client through `newClient`, built a real RunInstances request containing a marker Tailscale authentication key, invoked `RunInstance`, and returned in-process 307 responses without opening network sockets.

The unchanged production path replayed an identical POST body and `X-TC-Token` to an unrelated hostname. A subdomain and the original hostname on a different port received the body, `X-TC-Token`, and `Authorization`. Decoding the generated UserData before dispatch confirmed that it contained the Tailscale authentication key.

The focused redirect test passed together with the existing upstream RunInstances request-building and Tencent Cloud signing tests. The first test attempt was blocked only by an inaccessible default Go build-cache location; rerunning with a writable build cache passed. No deployed service, account, credential, or external network target was contacted.
